st.headline: China inflation slows in July, below forecast
st.teaser: The consumer price index eased to 0.5 per cent year-on-year.
fullText: BEIJING – China’s consumer and factory prices grew slower than expected in July , official data showed on Aug 9 , as the world’s second-largest economy confronts persistent deflationary pressure.
The consumer price index, a key gauge of inflation, eased to 0.5 per cent year-on-year, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
That was lower than the 0.8 per cent forecast by a Bloomberg survey and the slowest rise since January.
Sluggish domestic consumption has vexed Beijing for several years, threatening to weigh down national growth even as exports and certain high-tech sectors boom.

Many economists contend that China must shift towards a growth model driven more by household spending than the traditional engines of past decades, including real estate and infrastructure investment.
A gauge of China’s factory-gate prices, which measures the cost of goods at the first point of sale, also grew at a slower pace in July , NBS data showed on Aug 9 .
The producer price index increased 3.5 per cent year-on-year in July, slowing from 4.1 per cent in June and lower than the 3.8 per cent forecast by Bloomberg.
“Economic momentum softened in (the second quarter)“ of 2026, wrote Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist of Pinpoint Asset Management, in a note on the data on Aug 9 .

A meeting of the ruling Communist Party’s high-ranking Politburo in late July “ signalled stronger fiscal spending as the policy response”, wrote Zhang, adding that a couple of months are needed to assess how it may boost domestic demand.
The latest figures come two days after trade data for July showed exports and imports soaring, boosted by increased overseas demand for AI-related tech products.
The surge in exports in 2026 has helped China’s vast manufacturing sector through the prolonged slump in domestic spending. AFP

cna.headline: Jaissle begins Newcastle rebuild with Valencia win, Elanga scare not serious
cna.teaser: Jaissle begins Newcastle rebuild with Valencia win, Elanga scare not serious
fullText: Aug 9 : Newcastle United's new coach Matthias Jaissle sees plenty of work ahead for his young team after marking his first game in charge with a 2-1 pre-season friendly win over Valencia on Saturday.

Jaissle endured an early setback when Filip Ugrinic fired Valencia ahead inside four minutes, but Newcastle fought back at the Mestalla Stadium with substitute Yoane Wissa scoring twice in the second half.
"It was a friendly today. We will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot," Jaissle told reporters.
"We're quite balanced. We know what it is about. Now it's pre-season, and we're still looking to work on it. It's just a journey."
However, Jaissle said the Sweden international appeared to have escaped a serious injury.
"It seems to be not bad, so we are pleased. I hope it's true, then he can start again next week," the 38-year-old said.
"I was in fear, definitely, but now I'm more relaxed as the medical department is showing almost green lights, and there's nothing serious."
Jaissle, appointed on Wednesday following the departure of Eddie Howe, has inherited a squad in transition following the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.
The German manager turned to youth, with goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, midfielder Aladji Bamba and winger Bazoumana Toure making their debuts, while 18-year-old Sean Steur impressed off the bench.
"Time is the key. They're young lads," Jaissle said. "It's never going to be easy in football, especially at the highest level, but we're here to help them."
Newcastle begin their Premier League campaign against Liverpool on August 23.

listening.title: Solar Powering Singapore's Heartlands
listening.transcript: Singapore is ramping up solar panel installations across public housing estates to achieve its green energy goals. The Housing and Development Board plans to install solar panels on thousands of HDB blocks by 2030. While our tropical climate offers abundant sunlight, unpredictable cloud cover remains a key challenge for consistent power generation. Engineers are now trialing smart energy storage systems to bridge the gap during rainy periods.

economistArticle.title: The Tech Shield: India’s IT Sector Survives the AI Storm
paras: For the past eighteen months, a dark cloud of anxiety has hovered over Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Chennai. The rise of generative artificial intelligence was widely predicted to decimate India’s software-services industry, an export powerhouse that employs more than five million people. Pundits warned that cheap code-writing bots would render the country’s army of junior programmers obsolete overnight, collapsing the business model of tech giants like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys.

Yet, instead of a sudden, catastrophic collapse, the bellwethers of Indian IT are proving surprisingly resilient. Recent financial results show that while growth has slowed, revenues are holding up and profit margins remain robust. Rather than being swept away, Indian firms are absorbing the technology. They are rapidly retraining hundreds of thousands of employees to use AI tools, turning potential disruption into an internal productivity boost.

The primary casualties of this transition, however, are not the incumbent workers but rather the next generation of talent. The path to an entry-level tech job has become significantly steeper. Historically, Indian IT giants recruited tens of thousands of fresh engineering graduates annually, putting them through intensive training bootcamps. Today, because AI can automate basic debugging and routine coding, firms have drastically scaled down campus recruitment. Fresh graduates are finding that the bottom rungs of the career ladder have been kicked away.

To survive this paradigm shift, India’s IT behemoths are restructuring their offerings. Clients in America and Europe no longer want to buy cheap programming hours; they want complex, AI-driven solutions that integrate with their legacy systems. This requires Indian firms to move up the value chain, transitioning from low-cost coding hubs to sophisticated technology consultants. Contracts are being redrawn to focus on outcomes rather than headcount.

Ultimately, India's IT sector is surviving AI by evolving faster than expected. But this survival comes with a sober political reality. The industry can no longer act as the country's primary engine for mass middle-class job creation. While tech corporate profits may remain secure, the social contract that transformed millions of lower-income students into high-earning white-collar professionals is undergoing a painful rewrite.
economistArticle.cn:
在过去十八个月里，一团焦虑的乌云一直笼罩在班加罗尔、海得拉巴和金奈上空。人们普遍预测，生成式人工智能的崛起将重创印度的软件服务业，这是一个雇用了500多万人的出口支柱产业。权威人士警告说，廉价的写代码机器人将使该国庞大的初级程序员群体一夜之间被淘汰，从而导致塔塔咨询服务公司（TCS）和印孚瑟斯（Infosys）等科技巨头的商业模式走向崩溃。

然而，印度IT行业的风向标企业并没有出现突然的灾难性崩溃，反而表现出了令人惊讶的韧性。最近的财报显示，虽然增速有所放缓，但其收入依然维持，利润率也保持强劲。印度企业不仅没有被冲垮，反而正在吸收这项技术。他们正在迅速对数十万名员工进行AI工具培训，将潜在的颠覆转化为内部生产力的提升。

然而，在这场转型中，首当其冲的受害者并不是在职员工，而是下一代人才。进入入门级科技职位的门槛已经变得明显更高。历史上，印度IT巨头每年都会招聘数万名应届工程毕业生，并对他们进行密集的入职培训。如今，由于AI可以自动完成基础的调试和常规编码，企业已大幅缩减了校园招聘。应届毕业生发现，职业阶梯的底层已经被踢掉了。

为了在这场范式转变中生存下来，印度的IT巨头正在重组他们的产品与服务。美欧客户不再想购买廉价的编程工时，而是想要与他们遗留系统相整合的、复杂的AI驱动解决方案。这要求印度企业向价值链上游移动，从低成本的编码中心转型为成熟的技术咨询公司。合同正在被重新拟定，重点放在成果上，而非员工人数。

最终，印度的IT部门正通过比预期更快的进化速度在AI时代存活下来。但这种生存也伴随着冷酷的政治现实。该产业已无法再作为该国创造中产阶级就业的主要引擎。虽然科技企业的利润可能依然稳固，但曾让数百万低收入学生转变为高薪白领专业人士的社会契约，正在经历一场痛苦的重写。

gems.why: This sentence uses an introductory contrast ('Instead of...') followed by strong descriptive language ('catastrophic collapse') to debunk popular narratives before presenting the reality. / 该句通过引入对比句型（'Instead of...'）和强烈的描述性词汇（'catastrophic collapse'，意为灾难性崩溃），在呈现真实情况前，先有力地反驳了普遍存在的流行观点。
